blocks.text:
Estimate whether Proofpress improves a successor agent's admission of an APEX
professional artifact, relative to a realistic ordinary colleague handoff, and
whether any admission gain carries through to native downstream artifact
quality.

One Agent A works once in the complete frozen APEX Law world. At the handoff
checkpoint A emits the current DOCX, one ordinary handoff of at most 120 words,
and a private structured capture of decisions actually made. The same frozen A
checkpoint feeds every receiver arm; A is never rerun by arm.

- C0 receives the current artifact only.
- C1 receives the artifact and A's unedited natural handoff.
- C2 receives the identical artifact and byte-identical natural handoff, plus a

native portable Proofpress trail, decision/evidence links, artifact binding,
  DOCX provenance evidence, and the verification tool.

The task, artifact, receiver instruction, source-access boundary, model, tools,
and budget are fixed within each matched comparison. C2's additional
provenance and verification are the treatment, so decision fields are not
copied into C1 prose. No receiver-visible file may contain an arm, condition,
fault label, expected action, or oracle answer.

Before editing, B must freeze `Admission Decision.json`: selected artifact,
proceed/reverify/stop disposition, visible basis, and integrity status. The
primary outcome is deterministic admission correctness against a hidden oracle.
Unsafe continuation from a stale or binding-invalid artifact is reported
separately.

After a correct proceed decision, B creates the final SPA and change log. The
secondary outcome is the frozen nine-cell operative-section audit, with native
APEX grading, unrelated-clause regressions, completion, cost, latency, and tool
use reported separately. Fault cells have no DOCX denominator; a correct safe
stop is not scored as zero task quality.

The first qualification is one shared A checkpoint followed by six cells: C0,
C1, and C2 under clean and stale-binding states. Deterministic gates first prove
natural-handoff validity, C1/C2 byte identity for the common artifact and
summary, additive C2-only Proofpress files, no oracle leakage, native clean
verification, native fault detection, and scorer fixtures.

Every model cell is then inspected for admission-before-edit ordering, output
contract, actual carrier use, source leakage, and downstream scoreability. An
infrastructure failure is retained and may be retried in a new immutable root.
A design, leakage, scorer, or task failure invalidates that protocol version;
the fixture or harness is repaired and requalified under a new version rather
than silently replacing the observation.

No formal matrix begins unless C1 and C2 both complete the clean task, C2
verification succeeds on clean and fails on the binding fault, the hidden
oracle remains inaccessible, admission is written before downstream edits, the
ordinary handoff is useful but does not reproduce the complete Proofpress
record, and the downstream scorer has eligible non-ceiling error space.

After qualification, freeze task and world hashes, Agent A outputs, package and
scorer hashes, model/provider settings, repeats, ordering, retry/exclusion
rules, and a cost ceiling. Run independent receiver cells at the maximum
concurrency that does not share mutable APEX/Docker state. Preserve every
attempt and analyze paired C2-C1 admission correctness first, then clean
non-inferiority and downstream artifact quality.

The result is an APEX-derived Artifact Handoff Track, never an official APEX
leaderboard score. A positive result supports a bounded product claim about
portable, verifiable artifact admission and continuation under the tested
handoff boundary. A null or negative result is retained. Integrity verification
does not certify the legal truth of Agent A's admitted decisions.
